title: Prasorizo
subtitle: Greek leek and rice cooked in olive oil
excerpt: Leeks and rice cooked together slowly in olive oil and a little stock until the leeks are silky and the rice is soft. A simple Greek ladera dish that works as a main or a side.
sourceNotes: Greek ladera tradition, winter variant using leeks as the main vegetable.

recipe.batchNotes: Scales well. Use a wider pan to keep an even layer.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best served on the day. Leftovers keep for two days in the fridge and reheat with a splash of water.

content.text: Prasorizo is leek and rice cooked down together in olive oil. The leeks go very soft and sweet; the rice absorbs the stock and oil. Stir in lemon juice at the end to lift the whole dish.

items.prepNote: white and pale green parts, sliced into 1cm rounds

content.text: Warm the olive oil in the saucepan over a medium heat. Add the onion with a pinch of salt. Cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the leeks and stir to coat in the oil. Cook for 10 minutes, stirring often, until they wilt and soften.
Add the rinsed rice and stir for 1 minute so it is coated in the oil.
Pour in the hot stock. Season with salt and pepper. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and cook on a low heat for 20 minutes until the rice has absorbed the stock.
Remove from the heat. Stir in the lemon juice and dill. Put the lid back on and rest for 5 minutes.
Taste and adjust the salt. Serve warm with extra lemon wedges alongside.

items.symptom: The rice is still hard after 20 minutes.
items.cause: The heat was too low or the lid was not on tightly.
items.fix: Add 100ml of hot water, replace the lid and cook for another 8 minutes on a slightly higher heat.

items.cause: The rice was not rinsed and released excess starch.
items.fix: Rinse the rice under cold water until the water runs clear before cooking next time.

items.cause: They were not given enough time to wilt before the stock went in.
items.fix: Return to the heat with a splash of water and cook covered for a further 10 minutes.
